question: A 61-year-old female with a history of breast cancer currently on chemotherapy is brought by her husband to her oncologist for evaluation of a tremor. She reports that she developed a hand tremor approximately six months ago, prior to the start of her chemotherapy. The tremor is worse at rest and decreases with purposeful movement. She has experienced significant nausea and diarrhea since the start of her chemotherapy. Her past medical history is also notable for diabetes and hypertension treated with metformin and lisinopril, respectively. She takes no other medications. On examination, there is a tremor in the patient’s left hand. Muscle tone is increased in the upper extremities. Gait examination reveals difficulty initiating gait and shortened steps. Which of the following medications is contraindicated in the management of this patient’s nausea and diarrhea?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Patient has a history of breast cancer" -> "Currently undergoing chemotherapy" -> "Experiencing nausea and diarrhea" -> "Tremor present in left hand" -> "Tremor worse at rest, decreases with movement" -> "Increased muscle tone in upper extremities" -> "Difficulty initiating gait and shortened steps" -> "Symptoms suggest possible Parkinsonism" -> "Metoclopramide can exacerbate Parkinsonian symptoms" -> "Metoclopramide is contraindicated" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Patient is 61 years old" -> "Has a history of breast cancer" -> "On chemotherapy" -> "Developed hand tremor six months ago" -> "Tremor characteristics suggest Parkinsonism" -> "Nausea and diarrhea are side effects of chemotherapy" -> "Metoclopramide is used for nausea" -> "Metoclopramide can worsen tremors" -> "Metoclopramide is contraindicated" -> 90%

CHAIN: "Patient presents with tremor and gait issues" -> "Tremor is worse at rest" -> "Increased muscle tone noted" -> "Symptoms align with Parkinsonism" -> "Chemotherapy can cause nausea and diarrhea" -> "Metoclopramide is a prokinetic agent" -> "Metoclopramide can lead to worsening of Parkinsonian symptoms" -> "Metoclopramide is contraindicated" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Patient has nausea and diarrhea from chemotherapy" -> "Tremor and gait issues suggest possible Parkinsonism" -> "Metoclopramide is indicated for nausea" -> "Metoclopramide can worsen Parkinsonian symptoms" -> "Metoclopramide is contraindicated" -> 75%
analysis: The patient presents with a resting tremor, increased muscle tone, and gait difficulties, which are suggestive of Parkinsonism. Metoclopramide is a dopamine antagonist that can exacerbate Parkinsonian symptoms and is therefore contraindicated in this patient. Other options like ondansetron, benztropine, diphenhydramine, and loperamide do not have the same contraindication in this context.
